STL Scale Inspector
Know the Exact Size Before You Print

Stop wasting filament and resin on mis-sized files. Pick the scale your STL was modeled in and the scale you need — get the exact percentage to type into your slicer. Tested with digital calipers on a Bambu Lab A1 Mini.

No uploads, no accounts, no cookies. Use the scale math below, or drop an STL into the file inspector to read its real millimetre and inch dimensions on your own hardware.

Tested on Bambu A1 Mini•My Methodology

Conversion logic assumes a 175 human baseline. Eye Level measures to 160cm. Top of Head accounts for hair and helmets at 175cm.
Tip: Always use Uniform Scaling (lock X, Y, Z axes) in your slicer to avoid model distortion.

How I check scale before every print

  1. 1

    Find the sculptor's scale

    Check what scale the file was modeled in — usually listed on the download page or store page of the creator.

  2. 2

    Copy the exact percentage

    Eyeballing percentages leads to distorted proportions. The inspector gives exact mathematical output verified with physical calipers.

  3. 3

    Paste and lock axes

    Enter the percentage into your slicer, lock X, Y, and Z to uniform scaling, and slice.

The conversions I use most often

Before committing a miniature to a long print, verify the scale first. These are the percentages used in my own printing queue.
